extraction.reason: 1042 text row(s) were reconstructed across 77 page(s) and none formed a run of 3+ rows with a consistent column count. LIMITS OF THIS LAYER, so this is read as what it is: no ruling-line detection, no spanned-cell merging, no table joined across a page break. A grid with any of those shapes is a rung this layer does not reach yet.

authorities.owed: PARSE AND NORMALIZE. Two named unknowns, and neither is a fact about New Hampshire: (1) the pages are ROTATED, so the generic table layer reads each COLUMN as one row and returns ZERO_ROWS — an axis-swapped positional parse is the adapter that is owed, and the office heading / county section / candidate row segmentation is its unsolved half; (2) this repository holds NO SOURCED CROSSWALK from a New Hampshire State Representative district or Executive Council district to an OCD division. `data/states/nh/ballot/nh-merrimack-2026.json` carries exactly one such id (sldl:607, Merrimack District 7) and one data point is not a scheme. Deriving the rest would be inventing division ids, so the corpus is not wired into the reader projection until the crosswalk is acquired from its own authority.

authorities.owed: PARSE AND NORMALIZE, and then acquire the OTHER HALF OF NEW JERSEY. This document is the Division's complete applicable universe for the offices it is the filing officer for — federal — and that is not New Jersey's candidate universe. Every county, municipal, school and fire-district candidacy is filed with and published by ONE OF 21 COUNTY CLERKS, which is where data/states/nj/ballot/nj-morris-2026.json's 276 candidacies come from. NJ therefore cannot be labelled statewide by acquiring this alone (R-C9): the state universe is the UNION of this document and 21 county-clerk publications.
